body_ar:
حكم أمر المرأة بالمعروف ونهيها عن المنكر

هل يجوز أمر المرأة بالمعروف ونهيها عن المنكر؟

نعم، بل يجب عليها أن تأمر بالمعروف وتنهى عن المنكر، ويجب كذلك أمرها هي يجب على الرجال إذا رأوا من النساء منكرا أن ينهوا عن المنكر وأن يأمروا بالمعروف، وقد كان رسول الله (ص) يباشر ذلك، ففي الصحيحين أنه خطب خطبة العيد فظن أنه لم يسمع النساء فتوكأ على بلال فوقف على النساء ووعظهن وقال يا معشر النساء تصدقن فإني رأيتكن أكثر أهل النار، فبكى النساء فألقى بلال ثوبه فجعل النساء يهوين بأيديهن إلى حليهن ويرمينه في ثوب بلال.

---------------------------------------------------------

حكم بعض الأذكار غير الواردة عن رسول الله r والمرتبطة بمناسبات

هنا ورقة كتب فيها أذكار وهي توزع مصورة وفيها أنها تسبيح شهر رمضان واليوم الأول يقال فيه: سبحان من سبحت له السماوات بأطرافها مائة مرة؟

أن هذا النوع هو من الابتداع ومما لم يأذن به الله ولم يأت به رسول الله (ص) فلذلك لا بد من هجرانه وتركه وفيما جاء به رسول الله (ص) غنية عن مثل هذا...

-------------------------------------------------------------

حكم تعليق التمائم

هل معلق التميمة مشرك؟

هذا شرك أصغر ليس شركا أكبر، إلا إذا اعتقد أنها تنفعه وترفع عنه الضر فذلك شرك أكبر بالاعتقاد، لكن مجرد تعليقها شرك أصغر غير مخرج من الملة كالحلف بغير الله ونحو ذلك فإن النبي (ص) قال: من تعلق تميمة وكل إليها، وقال: من تعلق تميمة فلا أتم الله له، وقال: من تعلق شيئا وكل إليه، وقال كذلك: إن الرقى والتمائم والتِّوَلَة شرك، فالمقصود بذلك شرك دون شرك وهو لا يخرج من الملة.

-------------------------------------------------------------

حكم لكزانة

ما حكم ما يسمى بالكزانة أيا كان نوعها؟

أن الغيب قد استأثر الله به، وقال: ﴿عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا﴾، وقال: ﴿قل لا يعلم من في السماوات ومن في الأرض الغيب إلا الله﴾، وقد بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن مفاتيح الغيب وهي مقاليد الغيب خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله، والله تعالى يقول: ﴿وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو﴾، وهذه الخمس: ﴿إن الله عنده علم الساعة وينزل الغيث ويعلم ما في الأرحام، وما تدري نفس ماذا تكسب غدا وما تدري نفس بأي أرض تموت﴾،

ومحاولة التطلع عليها كأن يريد الإنسان الإطلاع على أجله أو على رزقه وما يرزق غدا، أو على وقت نزول المطر أو مجيء الغائب أو نحو ذلك فهذا من الكبائر، وصاحبه ربما أصيب بالفتن نسأل الله السلامة والعافية، كثيرا ما يكون المتطلع إلى ذلك عرضة للفتن فيسلط عليه الجن، ويفتن في دينه، والفتنة في الدين هي شر البلاء، شر البلية البلاء في الدين، والذي يبتلى في دينه يظهر له بعض الصدق فيما يخبر به الجان، أو ما يطلع عليه عن طريق هذه الوسائل، فيفتن بذلك ويظن أن كل ما يخبر به عن هذا الوجه صدق، فيتبع ذلك السبيل المظلم وبذلك تزل قدم بعد ثبوتها ويضل عن سواء الصراط نسأل الله السلامة والعافية.

يجب على المؤمن أن يستسلم لقدر الله خيره وشره، وأن يؤمن بذلك، وأن يعلم أن ما أصابه لم يكن ليخطئه وأن ما أخطأه لم يكن ليصيبه، وأنه رفعت الأقلام وجفت الصحف عما هو كائن، وأنه لا يقع في الكون شيء إلا بأمر الله وتدبيره، فيرضى حينئذ بكل ما كتب له، ولا يكون حينئذ صاحب تطلع إلى ما حجب عنه، وكلما كان الإنسان أوثق صلة بالله وأقوى إيمانا به كلما زهد في البحث عن المغيبات والأمور التي لا يطلع عليها.

وأعرف شيخا كبيرا من العلماء وهو الشيخ محمد يَبْرَ ولد بيه رحمة الله عليه كان أصم لا يسمع، وإنما يكتب له محدثه في الهواء فيفقه بالكتابة، فكتبت له: أن جهازا يوضع على الأذن يمكن عن طريقه السمع، وأني مستعد لأن أوفره له، فقال: أنا لا أريد أن أطلع على ما كتم ربي عني، فلم يرض أبدا باستعمال هذا الجهاز مع أنه من الأمور الجائزة، وليس من التطلع على الغيبيات، لكن من أهل العلم من يبلغ مستوى من التوكل على الله سبحانه وتعالى يظن أن هذا النوع من المعالجة هو مثل الكي، والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما أحب أن أكتوي»، فيصل إلى هذا المستوى،

ولذلك فالكزانة إذا كانت هي الخط، فقد كان نبي من أنبياء الله في الماضي يخط، فمن وافق خطه خط ذلك النبي فلا بأس، وإلا فلا خير فيها، كما بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك، ونحن الآن لا نستطيع أبدا أن نجزم بأن أي شيء منها موافق لما كان ذلك النبي يخطه، لأنه لا إسناد لنا في ذلك، فدل ذلك على حرمة الإشتغال بها مطلقا بجميع أنواعها وجميع هيئاتها، وأنه لا يحل التطلع على الغيبيات مطلقا بأي وسيلة من الوسائل.
body_en:
The ruling on enjoining right and forbidding wrong where a woman is concerned

Is it permissible for a woman to enjoin right and forbid wrong?

Yes; rather she is obliged to enjoin right and forbid wrong. And it is likewise obligatory that right be enjoined upon her: it is obligatory upon men, if they see a wrong among the women, to forbid the wrong and to enjoin the right. The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, used to undertake that himself. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs: he delivered the Eid sermon, and thought that the women had not heard him, so he leaned upon Bilal and stood over the women and admonished them, and said: 'O company of women, give charity, for I have seen you to be the majority of the people of the Fire.' So the women wept, and Bilal spread out his garment, and the women began reaching with their hands to their jewellery and throwing it into Bilal's garment.

------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on certain remembrances not transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ and tied to particular occasions

Here is a sheet with remembrances written on it, distributed as photocopies, and on it is that this is the glorification for the month of Ramadan, and that on the first day one says, a hundred times: 'Glory be to the One whom the heavens glorify with their farthest reaches.'

This kind of thing is innovation (bidʿah), and is among what God has not given leave for and what the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, did not bring. For that reason it must be abandoned and left, and in what the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, brought there is sufficiency to dispense with the like of this...

------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on hanging amulets

Is the one who hangs an amulet an associator of partners with God?

This is lesser association (shirk aṣghar), not greater association — unless he believes that it benefits him and lifts harm from him, in which case that is greater association, by virtue of the belief. But merely hanging it is lesser association, which does not take one out of the religion, like swearing by other than God and the like. For the Prophet, upon whom be peace, said: 'Whoever hangs an amulet is consigned to it'; and he said: 'Whoever hangs an amulet — may God not bring anything to completion for him'; and he said: 'Whoever hangs anything is consigned to it'; and he likewise said: 'Incantations, amulets and love-charms are association.' What is meant by that is an association below association, and it does not take one out of the religion.

------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on al-kazānah

What is the ruling on what is called al-kazānah, of whatever kind it may be?

God has kept the unseen to Himself. He said: {Knower of the unseen; and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone} (Sūrat al-Jinn 72:26). And He said: {Say: none in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God} (Sūrat al-Naml 27:65). The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear that the keys of the unseen — which are the locks of the unseen — are five, which none knows but God. And God, exalted, says: {And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He} (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:59). And these five are: {Indeed, God — with Him is knowledge of the Hour; and He sends down the rain; and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die} (Sūrat Luqmān 31:34).

Attempting to look into them — as when a person wants to know his appointed term, or his provision and what he will be provided with tomorrow, or the time the rain will fall, or the coming of one who is absent, or the like — this is among the grave sins. Its perpetrator may well be struck with trials; we ask God for safety and well-being. Very often the one who seeks to look into that becomes exposed to trials, so that the jinn are set upon him and he is tried in his religion. Trial in one's religion is the worst of afflictions; the worst of calamities is calamity in religion. The one who is tried in his religion has some truth appear to him in what the jinn tell him, or in what he comes to know by these means, and so he is put to trial by it and supposes that everything he is told from that quarter is true; and so he follows that dark path, and by it a foot slips after being firm, and he strays from the evenness of the way — we ask God for safety and well-being.

The believer is obliged to submit to God's decree, its good and its evil, and to believe in that; and to know that what has befallen him could not have missed him and what has missed him could not have befallen him; and that the pens have been lifted and the pages have dried over what is to be; and that nothing occurs in the universe except by God's command and His ordering. Then he is content with everything that has been written for him, and is not one who reaches after what has been veiled from him. The more firmly bound a person is to God, and the stronger his faith in Him, the less he cares to search out things of the unseen and matters he is not given to know.

I know a great old scholar, Shaykh Muhammad Yabra Ould Bayyah, God's mercy be upon him, who was deaf and could not hear; whoever spoke with him would write for him in the air, and he would understand by the writing. I wrote to him that there is a device placed on the ear by means of which hearing is possible, and that I was ready to provide it for him. He said: I do not wish to come to know what my Lord has kept from me. He never consented to use this device, even though it is among the permissible things and is not a matter of seeking to look into things of the unseen; but among the scholars there are those who reach a level of reliance upon God, glorified and exalted, at which they hold this kind of treatment to be like cauterisation — and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'I do not like to be cauterised.' So he reaches this level.

Therefore al-kazānah, if it is the drawing of lines: a prophet among the prophets of God in the past used to draw lines, so whoever's drawing coincides with the drawing of that prophet, there is no harm in it, and otherwise there is no good in it — as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear. And we today can never assert with certainty that any of it coincides with what that prophet used to draw, because we have no chain of transmission for that. This indicates the prohibition of occupying oneself with it absolutely, in all its kinds and all its forms, and that it is not lawful to seek to look into things of the unseen at all, by any means whatsoever.

flags.arabic: هل يجوز أمر المرأة بالمعروف ونهيها عن المنكر؟
options: the ruling on enjoining right and forbidding wrong where a woman is concerned — keeping the ambiguity
is it permissible for a woman to enjoin right and forbid wrong?
is it permissible to enjoin right upon a woman and forbid her wrong?
flags.note: The Arabic genitive أمر المرأة is ambiguous between the woman as the one who enjoins and the woman as the one enjoined, and the Sheikh answers BOTH senses in a single breath: she is obliged to enjoin right, and it is obligatory that right be enjoined upon her. English cannot hold both in one clause, so the heading has been kept deliberately open and the body spells out the two halves as he does. A rendering that picks only one sense would lose half of his answer.

flags.arabic: غير الواردة عن رسول الله r
flags.context: the heading of the second item
options: read the stray 'r' as the honorific ﷺ lost in font conversion, and render it as such (done here)
reproduce the stray character as printed
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (style guide §11). A bare Latin 'r' stands where the honorific belongs. This is the well-known artifact of Arabic symbol fonts in which the glyph ﷺ is mapped to the character 'r'; the CMS has stored the character rather than the glyph. The stray letter is preserved in body_ar and rendered as the honorific in body_en. Worth checking corpus-wide, since the same font mapping will have produced the same artifact elsewhere.

flags.context: حكم لكزانة … ما حكم ما يسمى بالكزانة أيا كان نوعها؟
options: al-kazānah — the same Mauritanian term as al-gazzānah elsewhere in the corpus
flags.note: A third spelling of the same Hassaniya word: الگزانه in article 526, لكْزانَه in article 540, and الكزانة / لكزانة here. All three should be recognised as one term when the corpus is indexed. Note that the Sheikh's ruling here is firmer than in article 526: here he concludes that occupying oneself with it is prohibited absolutely, in every kind and form, because no chain to the prophet who drew lines survives.

flags.arabic: فلم يرض أبدا باستعمال هذا الجهاز مع أنه من الأمور الجائزة
flags.context: the anecdote about the hearing aid
options: keep the Sheikh's explicit statement that the device is permissible
render the anecdote without the qualification
render the anecdote as a recommendation
flags.note: IMPORTANT FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh tells this story in praise of the old scholar's reliance on God, but he states plainly, in the same sentence, that the hearing aid is among the permissible things and that using it is not a matter of prying into the unseen. Detached from that qualification the anecdote would read as a ruling against hearing aids, which is the opposite of what he says. The qualification must never be dropped in any excerpt or summary of this item.

flags.arabic: هذا شرك أصغر ليس شركا أكبر
options: lesser association (shirk aṣghar) / greater association (shirk akbar)
flags.note: CROSS-REFERENCE. In article 537 of this slice the Sheikh says of the same practice that the Prophet 'counted it as associating partners with God' and that hanging amulets is forbidden (ḥarām), without distinguishing the two degrees. Here he distinguishes them and states that merely hanging an amulet does not take a person out of the religion. The two answers are not in conflict but they read very differently in isolation, and neither has been adjusted to the other. A reviewer should decide whether the site links them.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Four separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as four separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept.
The second item breaks off with an ellipsis in the source ('غنية عن مثل هذا...'). The ellipsis has been reproduced; it is not a truncation introduced in extraction.

The Sheikh quotes the Qur'an in the fourth item without references; the references have been supplied in the English per house style and the Arabic has not been altered. The four hadiths on amulets in the third item are given without collection or grading, and none has been supplied.
'The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried' renders رفعت الأقلام وجفت الصحف, the formula of the hadith on the decree; the Sheikh gives it without attribution.
Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: الإطلاع and الإشتغال written with connecting hamzas, and the vowelled proper name محمد يَبْرَ ولد بيه.
